summary: IExpress package launches a renamed LuaJIT CLI and extensionless Lua script. The script tampers with AMSI/ETW and loads an encoded Donut shellcode carrying a .NET credential stealer consistent with AgentTesla.

chain.evidence: RT_RCDATA CABINET contains an LZX cabinet with exactly FNJHLNGMQYBMIRMQ.EXE and QMRIMBYQMGNLHJNF. RUNPROGRAM invokes cmd.exe, creates C:\ProgramData\YAK, copies both files and starts the EXE with the extensionless script as its argument. SHOWWINDOW is zero. No Authenticode signature is present; Microsoft version strings belong to the Wextract template.

Native x86 LuaJIT 2.1.0-beta3 CLI. Static entry/main dispatch, runtime strings, imports and COFF data are consistent with an interpreter; it has no standalone hostile findings. main at 0x461b50 initializes the Lua state and dispatches argv to the protected CLI path at 0x4021a0. Renaming a generic interpreter does not turn its capabilities into malware-specific traits.

Source has 66 large Lua-5.1 VM definition blocks around the active FFI code, decimal-escaped literals, randomized identifiers and a 361,918-character encoded string. Static lexical reduction preserves the active statements and removes only recognized VM definition blocks for inspection; this is an analysis view, not executable recovered source.

Loads CLR, locates AmsiScanBuffer/AmsiInitialize names by NtQueryVirtualMemory plus RtlCompareMemory, zeroes them through NtWriteVirtualMemory and restores protection. Separate routines load amsi/ntdll exports and write bytes 31 C0 C3 (xor eax,eax; ret) after VirtualProtect; ETW targets include EtwEventWrite/Full/Register and NtTraceEvent. It also restores/camouflages API entry bytes, resolves syscall stubs, clears debug registers, hides threads and adds allocation/metadata noise.

A table-selected ten-character substitution and string reversal recover Base64; the decoded first byte carries a rotation in a 94-character printable alphabet. Reversing that rotation recovers 271,435 shellcode bytes. The Donut instance begins after CALL rel32 and contains Chaskey-CTR encryption. The decoder matches the upstream Chaskey test vector, recovers an instance with 63 API entries, and reads the embedded uncompressed NET_EXE module length to carve exactly 240,128 PE bytes.

The loader allocates an oversized native region, copies the decoded shellcode, appends NOP bytes, applies page transformations and PAGE_NOACCESS-style protection, installs a vectored access-violation handler, then casts the region to a function pointer. The handler reverses the page transformation on faults and permits execution. Actual success on a victim was not observed.

ILSpy statically decompiled the recovered assembly. The entry point configures permissive TLS certificate validation, runs the credential collector, starts configured keylogging/screenshot components, and enters an Application.Run loop. Browser and application collectors feed credential records into HTML reports delivered by SmtpClient. Windows Vault, Chromium login databases, Firefox key/login stores, Outlook, FileZilla, WinSCP and VPN stores are among the targets.

configuration: See evidence/payload-config.json. Keylogging and screenshots are enabled; clipboard/cookie/contact logging, Tor transport and startup installation are disabled. SMTP is configured for mail.outlook-office365.com:587 with TLS. The configured SMTP password is redacted in the review copy. No endpoint was contacted.
limitations: Static analysis only: no sample, Lua code, native helper or managed payload was executed.
The reduced Lua view is lexical and may retain dead routines; behavior is based on the original call path and inspected helper bodies, not on every API name appearing in a decoy table.
No exploitation or victim-side installation was observed. Startup capability is present in the managed code but disabled in this configuration.
engine_repairs: General IExpress SFX detection requires format resource names and a bounded plausible cabinet, then reuses existing extraction and recursive analysis. It does not infer hostility from the installer format.
Content sniffing skips a syntactically recognized long leading string assignment and scores the following source in a bounded window, without decoding or executing the string.
Lua decimal byte escapes are decoded with Lua semantics, consistently for literal values, imports and call arguments; other languages retain their existing escape semantics.
Facts output is treated as JSON even with the default output flag, preventing terminal sanitization from inserting invalid JSON escapes into decoded control characters.
Cleave’s literal corpus now calls the same language-aware decoder as filefacts, while retaining raw spellings for encoding rules and preserving Lua long-bracket raw strings.

taxonomy_review.placement: Neutral pointer writes, buffer fill, protection calls, memory compare/name references, sensitive API references and runtime paths remain in their corresponding micro-behavior leaves. Hostile composites live under AMSI or telemetry blinding, according to their required result.
taxonomy_review.evidence_bounds: The pointer-stub query binds the cast destination and all three indexed stores to the same variable. The buffer-fill query binds the allocated buffer and the loop index. The offensive composites state co-occurrence; they do not claim unproven source-to-sink bindings.
taxonomy_review.generalization: No filenames, C2 hosts, SMTP values, specimen hashes, campaign tokens or randomized identifiers gate a detector. Controls vary identifiers, decimal spellings and opcode/variable relationships. Far-separated reference controls exercise proximity.
taxonomy_review.packing_correction: The unsigned Microsoft-claim/inflated-data composite now requires high entropy in writable data itself. It can no longer borrow CAB compression entropy from .rsrc while claiming the small zero-filled .data is a hidden payload.
taxonomy_review.packing_positive_control: The synthetic control changes only .data entropy and disables CAB extraction to isolate root structural predicates from inherited LuaJIT framework findings; it retains the suspicious packing match. The unmodified wrapper has no such finding.
